analysis:
Integration pass over the GPT-OSS stop-string scoping change. Plumbing: ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope -> ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope -> GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope (opener `<|channel|>final`, openerEnd `<|message|>`, closers end/return/call/start). The scope flows through EngineV2SlotFactory.swift:574 -> EngineV2Config makeBridge -> EngineV2Bridge stored `let stopStringScope` (nil default) -> EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249-250 -> EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request -> CBv2Request.stopStringScope. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift replays StopHoldback(stopStrings:scope:) to report the matching candidate. The scope is hard-coded by model ID or type and is not derived from consumer input, so a consumer cannot choose or widen it. Consumers still supply only the stop strings, which they could already do.

Security effect: no change to TB-002 encryption or fail-closed handling (T-008), attestation or authorization (TB-011), or key handling. The prefix cache (T-041) is untouched: cacheScope/cacheSalt derivation, checkpoint scope, SSD gating, TTL and HMAC naming are unchanged, and the scope does not feed cache identity in any visible code. The change narrows stop matching, so it does not leak analysis text through stop truncation. It cannot suppress usage accounting in any visible code, because it only decides whether generation stops early.

Availability: a GPT-OSS model that never reaches the final channel now ends only on max_tokens, EOS or cancellation. max_tokens defaults to 4096 and the existing cancel path (T-010) is unchanged, so DoS exposure grows only marginally. Cost of the StopSequence replay is bounded by the generated text length and runs once at completion.

Coverage limits: the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (aee6ebb -> 38b90ed) contents were not supplied. That library implements CBv2StopStringScope and StopHoldback and runs in-process with decrypted prompts (TB-007, T-028), so the real engine-side scope handling, including partial-frame holdback and tool-call framing, is unreviewed. Docs, changelog and test changes are benign. This is an unverified contract and not a finding. A submodule-focused pass is advisable.
